ety.text: First recorded in the 1st Pskov manuscript. Often used in the 17th century. Inherited from Old East Slavic башта (bašta) from Italian bastia via Polish baszta or Czech bašta. The ending was influenced by the suffix -ня (-nja), which creates nouns of place, as in па́шня (pášnja), тамо́жня (tamóžnja). Doublet of Басти́лия (Bastílija) and бастио́н (bastión). Compare typologically опло́т (oplót), плете́нь (pleténʹ) (akin to плести́ (plestí)).
